# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct

## Our Pledge

We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our
community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body
size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender
identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status,
nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and
orientation.

## Our Standards

Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment include:

- demonstrating empathy and kindness;
- respecting differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences;
- giving and accepting constructive feedback;
- accepting responsibility, correcting mistakes, and learning from them;
- keeping technical disagreement focused on evidence and the work rather than the
  person.

Unacceptable behavior includes harassment, threats, targeted personal attacks,
doxxing, deliberate disclosure of private information, or sustained disruption of
project collaboration.

## Scope

This policy applies to participation in SemantIQ repository spaces and to conduct
that materially affects participation in the project.

Technical review, scientific disagreement, rejection of a proposal, or requests
for additional evidence are not conduct violations when expressed respectfully.

## Reporting conduct concerns

Do not post sensitive incident details, personal data, or private evidence in a
public issue.

For conduct occurring on GitHub, use GitHub's platform reporting and safety tools
where appropriate.

For non-sensitive questions about the process, open a public issue without
including incident details. If a private project-specific follow-up is necessary
and no private conduct channel is explicitly listed, ask maintainers only for a
private contact path.

The repository does not currently establish a dedicated private conduct mailbox.
Do not use the security-vulnerability contact for ordinary conduct disputes unless
the report also concerns a security vulnerability.

## Enforcement Responsibilities

The current repository maintainers are responsible for applying this policy within
project-controlled spaces. Depending on severity and available platform controls,
actions may include content moderation, requesting behavior changes, restricting
participation, or escalating to GitHub platform safety mechanisms.

Enforcement actions do not replace GitHub's own Terms of Service, Acceptable Use
Policies, or platform-level reporting processes.

## No retaliation

Good-faith reporting of conduct concerns, security issues, scientific
contradictions, or reproducibility failures must not be used as a basis for
retaliation within project-controlled review.
